landingSite.name: Blue Ghost Mission 1 landing site (Mare Crisium, near Mons Latreille)

segments.label: Launch & ascent — Kennedy Space Center LC-39A
segments.note: SpaceX Falcon 9 from Kennedy Space Center LC-39A (28.608°, -80.604°); ~9 min analytic ascent to a 185 km parking orbit (schematic arc, real pad and launch time).

segments.label: Parking orbit coast
segments.note: Circular 185 km parking orbit, inclination 36.0° (plane through the pad at launch and the Moon at arrival — the launch-window geometry). Coast 50 min to the injection burn into the phasing ellipse.

segments.label: Earth-orbit phasing loops
segments.note: Highly elliptical Earth orbits with apogee-raising burns at perigee (burn dates published by the provider; apogee values are modeled). The final loop is stretched so the last perigee passage coincides with the TLI time.

segments.label: Trans-lunar coast (5.6 days)
segments.note: Two-body Lambert arc from the TLI point to the modeled LOI point (Moon's position from the ephemeris at LOI). Departure Δv 75 m/s, arrival v∞ 0.82 km/s. Mid-course corrections not modeled.

segments.label: Lunar orbit (~102 km, 198.1 rev)
segments.note: Circular orbit after LOI (published 100 km; modeled 102 km so that the orbit reaches the descent-orbit-insertion point exactly at DOI). Plane contains the arrival asymptote and the landing site; inclination 66.3°.

segments.label: Descent orbit (102 × 20 km)
segments.note: Descent-orbit insertion lowers perilune to 20 km opposite the powered-descent point; 0.5 revolutions to PDI (DOI modeled at 2025-03-02T07:26:01Z, published 2025-03-02T07:50:00Z).

segments.label: Powered descent & landing
segments.note: Powered descent integrated for the lander class (Blue Ghost class (Firefly) — Mission 1 as flown: 2.6 kN, Isp 320 s, 1278 kg at PDI): 17.2 min, Δv 2077 m/s. Model, not telemetry. Published duration ≈11 min.

Touchdown — Blue Ghost Mission 1 landing site (Mare Crisium, near Mons Latreille) (18.560°, 61.810°)

notes: Route reconstructed from published event times and sites with two-body orbital mechanics — the shape between the anchors is a model, not flight telemetry.

Anchors: launch 06:11:39 UTC (KSC LC-39A, Falcon 9, rideshare with ispace Resilience); ~25 days of Earth-orbit phasing with two burns; TLI Feb 8; LOI Feb 13 8:51 pm EST (= Feb 14 01:51 UTC, 4 min 15 s) into ~150 × 5,673 km; circularised to ~100 km by Feb 24; DOI → ~30 min coast → 9-min PDI → touchdown Mar 2 08:34 UTC in Mare Crisium.
The capture orbit was elliptical and lowered over 16 days; the model draws a circular ~100 km orbit for that period.

Injection burn placed at 2025-01-15T07:10:45Z (published/nominal 2025-01-15T07:10:00Z): the perigee of the phasing ellipse is put where the final departure toward the Moon is tangential (apsidal drift over the phasing weeks is not modeled).
